p.src: The host asks how important leveraging the social-media following has been. Mitt answers that it has been huge, then immediately limits the scale of the claim. p.src:
The proof scene is a company-wide meeting. Six or seven new people were starting, and a director asked how they found the company and got the job. Mitt says that roughly $30\%$ to $40\%$ of the group answered that they had been following him or found the company through social media. With $N\in\{6,7\},
\qquad
p\approx 0.30\hbox{ to }0.40,$ the implied count is only approximate: $H\approx pN\approx (0.30\hbox{ to }0.40)(6\hbox{ to }7)\approx 2\hbox{ to }3.$ That arithmetic should stay modest. It is not a conversion rate from followers to hires. It is a way to keep the scale of the anecdote honest: in one small starting cohort, a few people reportedly entered the company’s awareness path through Mitt’s public content.

p.src:
In this lecture, hashtags are not treated as decoration. They are treated as routing signals. The speaker gives practical counts, $H_{\text{static post}}\approx 8\text{--}10,
\qquad
H_{\text{video/reel}}\approx 6,$ but the more important condition is relevance. If a post uses an investing hashtag and people who like investing content begin to engage, the platform has a cleaner guess about whom to test next. The speaker describes two possible surfaces: Explore distribution and homepage distribution to people who do not already follow the page.

It shows how one operator packages a Reel so that the content, discovery layer, description, and niche signals are all deliberately set before publishing.
